newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up in dull trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up in dull trading.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up on Wednesday due to short-covering but thin trading volumes indicated further falls were likely, traders said.
The most active April 1997 contract ended at 19,620 yuan ($2,364) per tonne, rising 80 yuan. It opened at 19,600 yuan, hitting an intra-day low of 19,590 and a high of 19,690.
January rose 150 to 19,630, February 100 to 19,630, March 90 to 19,620, May 120 to 19,650 and June 80 to 19,720.
Combined volume fell sharply to 39,710 tonnes from 110,480.
Copper opened higher on technical short-covering and consolidated at high levels for most of the session, traders said.

"Some wary retail investors offset their short positons and took profits first today," one trader said. "But thin volumes indicated most investors expected copper would continue its downward movement in the short term."
"Market sentiment did not improve despite today's technical rebound," a second trader said. "Short position holders have dominated trading since copper breached the key 20,000-yuan support level."
"Copper is likely to test the next key 19,000-yuan support level in the coming days due to weak market sentiment," he added.
Aluminium ended up. The only traded January contract rose 20 yuan to close at 13,900 yuan per tonne with turnover of 10 tonnes.
